summary: Pakistan issues tourist eVisas through its official online portal to around 175 nationalities — with fees currently waived for many of them — while a stricter list of countries must obtain a visa from a Pakistani embassy before travel. Indian passport holders face a highly restrictive special regime, and Israeli passports are not admitted at all.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months on arrival in Pakistan and have at least one blank page for the entry stamp.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) is required if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

vaccinations.name: Polio
vaccinations.text: Visitors staying longer than 4 weeks must show proof of polio vaccination (taken between 4 weeks and 12 months before departure) when leaving Pakistan. The vaccine is also available free at government facilities in Pakistan.

travelInsurance.text: Travel insurance is not a formal entry requirement, but comprehensive coverage including medical evacuation is strongly recommended — healthcare is limited outside the major cities.

onwardTicket.text: A return or onward ticket is not formally required for entry, but the eVisa application asks for travel details and airlines may ask to see a return booking.

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published. Border officers rarely ask, but the visa application may require bank statements, a hotel booking or an invitation letter from a licensed tour operator.

currencyLimits.text: Foreign currency worth more than USD 10,000 (or equivalent) must be declared on arrival, and taking large amounts of cash out of the country is restricted. Check current State Bank of Pakistan limits before travel.

notes: Alcohol may not be brought into Pakistan — imports are prohibited and duty-free purchases are confiscated at the border.
Drones require prior authorization and are regularly confiscated on arrival.
Narcotics offenses carry extremely severe penalties, including the death penalty.

payments.text: Cards work at upmarket hotels, chain stores and restaurants in Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad, but Pakistan largely runs on cash. Carry rupees for taxis, bazaars and everything outside the big cities.

safety.text: The main cities and northern tourist circuits (Hunza, Skardu) generally receive visitors warmly, but several governments advise against travel to areas near the Afghan border, parts of Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa because of terrorism risk. Check current advisories, stick to open areas and confirm whether your route needs a No Objection Certificate.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Pakistan Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: October to March brings cool, dry weather to the plains and cities; for the northern mountain valleys such as Hunza and Skardu, May to September is the season instead.

idp.text: Pakistan is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

driving.text: Pakistan is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Pakistan yet.

tips.text: Apply only through the official portal visa.nadra.gov.pk — third-party sites charge large markups. Most tourist applicants need a hotel booking or an invitation letter from a licensed Pakistani tour operator.

Some areas — parts of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, districts near the borders, and parts of Balochistan — are closed to foreigners or require special permits and sometimes an armed escort. Plan routes through open areas and check locally before leaving the main highways.
If you stay more than 4 weeks you must show a polio vaccination certificate when leaving Pakistan — get the vaccine before travel or free of charge at a government facility in Pakistan.
Dress conservatively — long trousers and covered shoulders; a headscarf is useful for women visiting mosques. During Ramadan, avoid eating, drinking or smoking in public in daylight hours.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Pakistan?
faq.answer: Almost everyone does. Around 175 nationalities can apply online for a tourist eVisa at visa.nadra.gov.pk — with the fee currently waived for many countries — while the remaining nationalities must apply at a Pakistani embassy, where applications go through additional clearance. Genuine visa-free entry is limited to a few bilateral arrangements.

faq.question: How long does the Pakistan eVisa take?
faq.answer: Most tourist eVisas are decided within about 7–10 working days, and many come through faster. Apply a few weeks ahead in case additional documents are requested, and use only the official visa.nadra.gov.pk portal.

faq.question: Can Indian citizens visit Pakistan as tourists?
faq.answer: Not in practice. Pakistan issues visas to Indian nationals almost exclusively for religious pilgrimages under the bilateral protocol, family visits and official travel, arranged through the Pakistani High Commission in New Delhi. Tourist visas are effectively unavailable, and visas that are issued are typically city-specific with police reporting requirements.

faq.question: Can I enter Pakistan on an Israeli passport?
faq.answer: No. Pakistan does not recognize Israel and does not admit travelers on Israeli passports. Dual nationals should travel on their other passport.

faq.question: Is Pakistan safe for tourists?
faq.answer: It depends heavily on where you go. The northern mountain areas and the main cities host growing numbers of tourists without incident, but several governments advise against travel to border regions, parts of Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Read your government's current advisory, register your trip and consider traveling with a reputable local operator.
